title: Tanzanian Chicken Coconut Soup
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Supu ya Kuku wa Nazi — chicken simmered in a fragrant coconut milk broth with ginger, garlic, lemon grass, and coriander. The coastal healing soup — light, fragrant, and deeply nourishing.
longDesc: Chicken coconut soup is the coastal Tanzanian healing food — lighter than the stew version, more brothy, and fragrant with lemon grass and coriander. Given to the sick and served as a starter at coastal celebrations.
steps: Simmer chicken with water, onion, garlic, ginger, lemon grass, and turmeric for 35—40 minutes.
Remove chicken. Shred finely. Discard lemon grass.
Add coconut milk to the broth. Simmer gently 8 minutes.
Season. Garnish with coriander. Serve with lime.
chefTips: Lemon grass must be bruised — cut or pound to release its aromatic oils.
Never boil after adding coconut milk.
Lime at the table brightens every bowl.
cookingScience: Lemon grass contains citral — a volatile aromatic compound released when the stalk is bruised and exposed to heat. Extended boiling destroys it; the brief simmer in step 2 preserves it.
sustainabilityTips: Local Tanzanian chicken and coastal coconuts.
culturalNote: Chicken coconut soup is the soup of the Tanzanian coast — given with love to the sick, served at celebrations, and eaten by families on cool evenings along the Indian Ocean shore.
